title: Two Minutes: Know When to Leave

scenes.title:
A fire.
A decision.
points: Is it still confined to the pan?
Or is it time to leave?
sentences: A kitchen fire can force a decision before you have time to search for instructions.
Is it still a small, confined pan fire, or is it time to leave?
Knowing a safety rule is different from recognizing the situation in front of you.
Two Minutes turns that decision into a short practice drill.

scenes.title:
Practise the
decision in space.
sentences: The Lens puts a virtual cooktop, lid, burner control and marked exit into your space.
Two starting conditions let you compare different decisions.
Leaving is available throughout.
This demonstration runs in Lens Studio's preview for Specs.

scenes.title:
A small,
confined pan fire.
points: Slide the lid from the side
Turn heat off if safely reachable
Keep the pan covered until cool
sentences: Here, the fire is confined to the pan.
I lift the lid at the side, slide it over the pan and switch off the front burner control.
The drill recognizes containment and reminds me to keep the pan covered until completely cool.
It never forces a correctly contained fire to spread for a dramatic ending.
If I have any doubt, leaving is still the right option.

scenes.title:
Beyond the pan?
Leave.
points: The lid cannot solve this scenario
sentences: In the second scenario, the fire has already spread beyond the pan.
Approaching the lid or burner cannot solve it.
I turn toward the virtual exit and choose to leave.
Outside in the drill, I can close the door when safe and simulate calling for help.
Leaving does not extinguish the fire.
The next action is to stay out.

scenes.title:
Make the mistake
here, in practice.
points: The debrief explains the actual choices
sentences: Water is an unsafe choice for a grease fire.
Selecting the virtual glass triggers a restrained consequence and an evacuation path.
I leave and call from outside.
The debrief explains why water was unsafe and records both the mistake and the recovery.
A reset clears the previous attempt.

scenes.title:
One state.
Consistent outcomes.
sentences: Planning used Devpost Learn.
The build uses CLAD, Lens Studio and the Lens Studio MCP.
SIK handles interaction, UIKit handles the views and one state machine owns every decision.
Twenty-three portable tests and seven native preview cases passed.

scenes.title:
Know when
to leave.
points: Device and learning studies come next
sentences: The kitchen and exit are virtual.
Real-glasses comfort and teaching effectiveness still need testing.
Two Minutes names the drill, not a safe amount of time to stay in a fire.
